Subject: Follow-up from today - deployment needs and numbers

Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying items so you can scope pricing: 

Summary of our needs
- Use case: realtime fraud detection and risk explanations surfaced in agent UI.
- Peak concurrency: ~80 qps inference calls, average tokens per request ~600 (prompt+response expected).
- Monthly volume: ~80M input tokens, ~60M output tokens (total ~140M tokens/month).
- Latency SLO: 200–300ms 95th for short paths (we understand longer for larger contexts).
- Security: data residency in US, SOC2+ required, possible on-prem for certain regulated flows.

Questions we flagged during the call
1) For these numbers, should we be looking at Hosted API with token pricing, Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity, or Private VPC/on-prem? Pros/cons for each for our use case?
2) What ballpark pricing should we expect for: (a) hosted per-token, (b) 1x dedicated pool (reserved commit) sized for 80 qps, (c) private VPC license model + on-prem sizing?
3) What engineering effort / timeline should we plan for a Dedicated vs Private deployment?

Attached is a short usage dump from our telemetry team (fintechco_usage_summary.xlsx) — hope that helps. We want a short internal decision doc by next Wed so would appreciate ballpark numbers + recommended next step by EOD Fri if possible.

Thanks,
Sarah

Thanks Sarah — great notes and the usage attachment is helpful. Quick recap from our side and proposed approach: 

High-level recommendation
- We'll start with a Hosted API pilot so you can validate latency/quality quickly (low time-to-value) while we size a Dedicated proposal in parallel. If regulatory gating appears, we can run a Private VPC evaluation based on the same usage profile.

Why this approach
- Hosted: fastest to ship, pay-as-you-go (per-token), no infra lead time. Good for initial validation and ML iteration.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput, lower unit cost at scale (reserved commits/month), required if you need consistent 95th latency and isolation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): recommended only if compliance/regulatory controls require customer-managed networking or HSM/KMS on-prem. Higher setup/time and license/infra cost.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Aditya: can you provide a Dedicated pool sizing + ballpark reserved-commit pricing and assumptions (GPU type, expected tokens/month, sustained qps) by EOD Thu?
2) Vivek: can you add notes on typical Private VPC on-prem timeline and one-time setup costs we should call out?
3) Marissa: I'll send a short one-pager (redwood_pricing_model.pdf) with hosted vs dedicated illustrative numbers and a suggested mutual action plan.

If that sounds good, Sarah — we'll target the cost numbers Friday and a quick follow-up call next Tue to walk through the options.

Best,

-----Original message-----
On Tue, Mar 2, 2026 at 9:10 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Sarah — great notes and the usage attachment is helpful. Quick recap from our side and proposed approach:
> 
> High-level recommendation
> - We'll start with a Hosted API pilot so you can validate latency/quality quickly (low time-to-value) while we size a Dedicated proposal in parallel. If regulatory gating appears, we can run a Private VPC evaluation based on the same usage profile.

Sizing assumptions (from fintechco_usage_summary.xlsx + call)
- Total tokens/month: 140M
- Average request tokens: 600
- Peak concurrency target: 80 qps
- Target 95p latency: <= 300ms for most flows

Ballpark economics (illustrative)
1) Hosted (per-token) — Redwood hosted API
- Example unit price: $0.00035 per input token, $0.00045 per output token (illustrative; final depends on model selection)
- Monthly cost estimate = (80M * 0.00035) + (60M * 0.00045) = $28,000 + $27,000 = $55,000/month
- Pros: no infra setup, immediate onboarding, automatic scaling.
- Cons: higher marginal cost at high volume, potential multi-tenant variability on tail latency.

2) Dedicated (reserved commit) — 1x dedicated pool sized for sustained 80 qps
- Typical reserved commit model: monthly fixed fee for GPU pool + per-request token metering at a lower unit price (or included in commit depending on tier).
- Rough estimate (depends on GPU type): $38k–$60k/month commit for pool sized to sustain 80 qps (N GPUs + autoscale buffer).
- If we assume a $45k/month commit and reduced per-token charge (or token-included up to commit), your effective unit economics could be ~30–40% lower than hosted at current volume.
- Pros: predictable latency, isolation, better unit cost at scale.
- Cons: contractual commit, longer procurement time, less flexible for bursts unless burst options added.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
- One-time onboarding + infra: depends heavily on on-prem hardware choices. Typical upfront professional services + license: $150k–$400k (one-time) + ongoing support/maintenance.
- Good when strict data residency, network controls, or HSM requirements exist.

Assumptions / caveats
- These are illustrative; we'll refine once you pick an expected model (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and confirm target SLA, model family (LlamaX / redwood-curie etc.), and token compressions/quantization.

Next steps (technical)
- I'll prepare a Dedicated sizing workbook that maps qps -> GPUs -> commit cost (ETA: EOD Thu).
- Vivek: please add Private deployment timeline/PS estimates inline to my sheet when you have a sec.
